title: Randomized controlled trial evaluating the impact of mineralocorticoid receptor blockade by eplerenone on echocardiographic abnormalities among kidney graft recipient under calcineurin inhibitors. KT-CANOPY : Cardiac improvement by eplerenone among patients under cyclosporine or tacrolimus for kidney transplantation.
official: Randomized controlled trial evaluating the impact of mineralocorticoid receptor blockade by eplerenone on echocardiographic abnormalities among kidney graft recipient under calcineurin inhibitors. KT-CANOPY: Cardiac improvement by eplerenone among patients under cyclosporine or tacrolimus for kidney transplantation.
summary: Main objective: To assess the impact of 36 weeks administration of eplerenone on a hierarchical composite endpoint including major cardiovascular events and cardiac structural changes in kidney transplant recipients for more than one year, receiving calcineurin inhibitors.
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Men or women ≥ 18 years of age.
2. Patient affiliated to a social security scheme or beneficiary of such a scheme.
3. Person who has undergone a prior clinical examination suitable for the clinical trial.
4. Renal transplant patient for at least one year.
5. Patient on long-term ciclosporin or tacrolimus therapy.
6. Patient with a clinical and biological situation stable for at least three months: no change in treatment with a potential impact on blood pressure for 3 months (excluding immunosuppressive therapy) and no acute graft rejection diagnosed within 3 months
7. Patient with a GFR estimated according to the CKD-EPI formula ≥40ml/min/1.73m2 less than one month old.
8. Patient with peripheral SBP≥110mmHg, regardless of whether or not antihypertensive treatment (including ACE inhibitor or sartan) is being used.
9. With the following echocardiographic abnormalities on trans-thoracic echocardiography performed at inclusion: - Indexed LV mass > 88 g/m2 in women or > 102 g/m2 in men, - And/or Left atrial volume > 34 ml/m2.
10. Patient signed informed consent.
Exclusion criteria:
1. Patient transplanted more than 5 years.
2. Patients treated with digoxin.
3. Left ventricular ejection fraction <40% on echocardiography at inclusion.
4. Planned ligature of the arteriovenous fistula in the coming year.
5. Known hypersensitivity or allergy to eplerenone and its excipients.
6. Patients with severe hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh class C).
7. Patient treated with a potent CYP3A4 inhibitor (e.g. itraconazole, ketoconazole, ritonavir, nelfinavir, clarithromycin, telithromycin and nefazodone).
8. Patients with known galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose or galactose malabsorption syndrome.
9. Patients with a contraindication to Kayexalate: history of hypersensitivity to polystyrene sulphonate resins, obstructive intestinal pathology or laxative treatment with sorbitol.
10. A woman of childbearing age without an effective contraceptive device : A woman is considered to be of childbearing age, i.e., fertile, from the onset of her first menstruation until she becomes menopausal, unless she is permanently sterile. An effective contraceptive method is considered to be: estrogen-progestogen hormonal contraception that inhibits ovulation, administered orally, intravaginally, or transdermally; or progestogen-only hormonal contraception that inhibits ovulation, administered orally, by injection, or implant; or intrauterine device (IUD) or hormonal IUD; or tubal ligation; or male partner with vasectomy; or sexual abstinence.
11. Women wishing to become pregnant within 12 months.
12. Patient in permanent atrial fibrillation.
13. Patient taking part in other therapeutic interventional research.
14. Pregnant woman, parturient or breast-feeding mother
15. Minor child (not emancipated)
16. An adult subject to a legal protection measure (guardianship, curatorship, safeguard of justice)
17. Persons deprived of their liberty by a judicial or administrative decision.
18. Patient unable to express consent.
19. Patient with valve disease grade 3 or higher.
20. A patient whose risk of mortality is considered to be very high in the following year.
21. Patients with documented kalaemia ≥ 5mmol/L in the month before or on long-term potassium chelating resins.
22. Blood bicarbonate level < 20mmol/L with or without documented supplementation in the month before.
23. Patient under mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist or with formal indication to receive this treatment.
24. Patient receiving another potassium-sparing diuretic.
25. Patients receiving a combination of ACE inhibitors and sartan.
